correctness.rationale: The twisted group-algebra decomposition yields \(q^{n-2s}\) irreducibles of degree \(q^s\) for each central weight. The Frobenius–Schur character average collapses to a quadratic Gauss sum because every group square is central. Polar radical translations and the finite-field Arf classification give 0/±1, with bilinear bipartite factorization yielding +1. An explicit inverting involution proves strong reality for bipartite graphs; weighted odd-cycle radical witness forces indicator zero in nonbipartite graphs. The \(K_4\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) sum gives −1. Independent exhaustive GF2/GF4 checks confirm small cases but are not relied on for infinite assertions.

value.rationale: Classifies a meaningful group-theoretic property (reality and strong reality) exactly in terms of graph bipartiteness for every graph and every even finite field. Provides the complete complex representation Frobenius–Schur type census by exact central-character strata, beyond degree and class counts. Odd cycles give a sharp nonreality obstruction; K4 exhibits genuinely quaternionic representations. Structural graph criterion and full indicator trichotomy are naturally reusable in finite-group representation theory.
